name: BSI TR-02102-2 (TLS)
reference: BSI TR-02102-2 'Cryptographic Mechanisms: Recommendations and Key Lengths, Part 2 – Use of Transport Layer Security (TLS)', version 2026-01: Table 2 (versions), Table 3 (PFS suites) + Table 4 (non-PFS (EC)DH suites) + Table 13 (TLS 1.3 suites), Tables 6/10 (Diffie-Hellman groups), Table 11 (signature algorithms), Table 14 (key lengths); §3.1.2 (120-bit security level).
summary: The German federal TLS baseline targeting 120-bit security. AES-only suites (no ChaCha20), NIST/Brainpool curves and ffdhe3072+ (no x25519), RSA-PSS/ECDSA signatures, RSA/DH >= 3000-bit.
notes: protocols.allow [tls1_2, tls1_3] from Table 2 ('TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.1 are not recommended', 'SSL v2 ... and SSL v3 ... are not recommended'). cipher_suites.allow is the verbatim union of Table 3 (recommended PFS suites), Table 4 (recommended non-PFS (EC)DH suites) and Table 13 (TLS 1.3): AES only, in CBC (with Encrypt-then-MAC), GCM or CCM. ChaCha20-Poly1305 is NOT in any table, so it is excluded -- a shape-tag rule could not do this. FLAG: Table 5 (PSK suites) is recommended by BSI but omitted here, as this scanner does not probe PSK; a PSK deployment should consult Table 5 directly. groups.allow from Tables 6 and 10: NIST secp256r1/384r1/521r1, the Brainpool curves (incl. their RFC 8734 tls13 code points) and ffdhe3072/4096; x25519 and x448 are NOT recommended by BSI and are excluded. signature_algorithms.allow from Table 11: RSA-PSS (rsae and pss) and ECDSA over the NIST curves; rsa_pkcs1_* are omitted because Table 12 recommends them only 'until 2025' (PKCS#1 v1.5), which has passed. minimum_security_strength 120 (§3.1.2 'is 120 bits'). certificate min_rsa_bits 3000 (Table 14 'RSA 3000 Bit'), min_ec_bits 250 (Table 14 'ECDSA 250 Bit'), disallow_sha1 (no SHA-1 in any BSI table). The recommended lists are much shorter than administrators expect; a typical server offering x25519 or ChaCha20-Poly1305 will not conform.
